basics.name: Alexander Phillips
basics.label: Principal Engineer, Test Engineering
basics.summary: Principal engineer in test engineering and silicon validation, focused on Cadence’s Palladium emulation and Protium prototyping systems. Ten years of building test-automation frameworks, system-monitoring software, and manufacturing tests for rack-scale hardware, starting from a physics background in dark-matter research.

work.name: Cadence Design Systems
highlights: Created the Protium System Manager (PTSM), which ships on every Protium X3 rack: it reports the live status of every blade and moved blade-to-blade communication from UART to Ethernet, a far more reliable link.
Built the automated test framework for the Palladium Z3 and Protium X3 rack-level designs, made R&D’s tests run more efficiently, and wrote new tests for several product lines.
Helped launch Palladium Z3 and Protium X3 into manufacturing.

work.name: Jabil Circuit
work.position: Test Engineering Lead, High Performance Computing
highlights: Led the department’s test group of engineers and technicians; promoted from intern to test engineering lead and certified as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) Engineer by examination.
Designed and maintained the automated test infrastructure for a customer’s enterprise emulation platform, and later a large-scale device-testing framework, in Python, Bash, and C shell on Linux.
Proposed and built a generative adversarial network (GAN) to detect defects in printed circuit boards.

Built production data tooling: test-result parsers in Python, Rust, and Go for the manufacturing execution system (MES), a live test-progress monitor for the factory floor, and a secure data portal spanning test stations.
Designed tests with customer engineers, traced design flaws, and consulted site-wide on new product introductions.

work.name: King Saud University
work.summary: Built dye-sensitized solar cells and measured their quantum efficiency.

work.name: Purdue University
work.position: Undergraduate Research Assistant, High Energy Physics
highlights: Developed pulse-shape discrimination methods in C and Python to separate neutron and gamma recoils in XENON100 detector data for dark-matter searches.
Built hardware for a neutron-generator setup, including a hardware replacement for gamma-recoil discrimination scripts.

education.area: Electrical and Computer Engineering, Minor in Physics
